saints.name: St. Nicholas of Tolentino
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: An Augustinian friar and preacher of Tolentino, famed for his charity and for his prayers for the souls in purgatory…
biography: Born in 1245 at Sant'Angelo in Pontano in the March of Ancona, Nicholas was named for Nicholas of Bari, at whose shrine his childless parents had prayed for a son. Drawn by the friars' preaching, he entered the Augustinian order about 1264, not long after its Grand Union of 1256, and was ordained priest around 1270.

Sent about 1275 to Tolentino, he served the town for thirty years as preacher, confessor, and visitor of the poor and sick, and was renowned in life for miracles. Once, weakened by long fasting, he was bidden in prayer to eat bread marked with a cross and dipped in water; the blessed 'bread of St. Nicholas' given to the sick from that day is still distributed on his feast.

Devoted above all to prayer for the dead, he became the Church's great intercessor for the souls in purgatory, whose patron he is. He died at Tolentino on 10 September 1305, and in 1446 Pope Eugene IV canonized him, the first friar of his order to be raised to the altars.
saints.knownFor: His preaching, his charity, and his intercession for the holy souls.
